lesson.title: Preparation and opening of the Divine Liturgy

readings.title: Office of Oblation
readings.text: (3) All this and the whole Office of Oblation are said while the clergy are vesting, in a low voice, by the Priest, behind the image-screen (ikonostás), which corresponds to the chancel-rail in the Western Church. At the point duly indicated, after the Priest and Deacon have vested themselves, the Reader (in front of the image-screen), begins to read the Hours; the Priest (behind the image-screen), making aloud the exclamations and benedictions, as shown in the Hours.

readings.title: Opening blessing
readings.text: Blessed is the kingdom of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, now, and ever, and unto ages of ages. Choir. Amen.

readings.title: Great Litany: petitions
readings.text: For the peace that is from above, and for the salvation of our souls, let us pray to the Lord. ℟ For the peace of the whole world; for the welfare of God's holy Churches, and for the union of them all: ℟ For this holy Temple, and for those who with faith, devoutness, and in the fear of God have entered therein: ℟

readings.title: Prayer of the First Antiphon
readings.text: O Lord our God, whose might is ineffable, whose glory is inconceivable, whose mercy is infinite, and whose love toward mankind is unutterable: Look down, O Master, in thy tender compassion, upon us and upon this holy Temple; and deal with us and with those people who here pray with us, according to the riches of thy mercies and thy bounties.

scripture.translation: KJV (public domain in the United States)
scripture.text: I exhort therefore, that, first of all, supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks, be made for all men; For kings, and for all that are in authority; that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty.

overview.text: The Divine Liturgy is the Church’s Eucharistic service. These opening selections distinguish the clergy’s preparation of the gifts, the public opening blessing and the shared petitions of a litany.
overview.reason: The owner authorized a plain-English curriculum explanation so beginners can understand the topic before consulting the preserved source passage.

readings.title: What is the Office of Oblation?

paragraphs.text: Oblation means offering. In Hapgood’s explanatory account, the clergy’s preparation behind the iconostasis overlaps with the reader’s recitation of the Hours. The iconostasis is the screen of icons separating the sanctuary from the main part of the church; the passage describes simultaneous parts of the published service.
paragraphs.reason: The owner authorized a plain-English curriculum explanation so beginners can understand the topic before consulting the preserved source passage.

readings.title: What does the opening blessing announce?

paragraphs.text: The opening blessing names the kingdom of the Father, Son and Holy Spirit. It places the service in a Trinitarian setting, and the choir’s Amen expresses the response printed in the order.
paragraphs.reason: The owner authorized a plain-English curriculum explanation so beginners can understand the topic before consulting the preserved source passage.

paragraphs.text: A litany is a series of prayer petitions with repeated responses. The quoted petitions of the Great Litany concern peace, salvation, the churches and the people assembled in the temple. The subjects show the breadth of the prayer, extending beyond the needs of one individual.
paragraphs.reason: The owner authorized a plain-English curriculum explanation so beginners can understand the topic before consulting the preserved source passage.

readings.title: What is expressed in the first antiphon prayer?

paragraphs.text: The prayer addresses God’s unlimited power and mercy and asks compassion for the assembled people. An antiphon is a sung section of the service; this prayer belongs to the first such section in the published order.
paragraphs.reason: The owner authorized a plain-English curriculum explanation so beginners can understand the topic before consulting the preserved source passage.

paragraphs.text: The linked resource concerns Prothesis, the preparation of the Eucharistic gifts. It accompanies the distinction made in Hapgood’s notes between that preparation and the public opening of the Liturgy.
